_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); gold-miner signals with Newmont's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'Newmont is one of the world’s largest gold producers and is the only gold company included in the S&P 500 Index and Fortune 500.' 'Our business is dependent on the prices of gold and copper, which fluctuate on a daily basis and are affected by numerous factors beyond our control.' 'A substantial or extended decline in gold or copper prices would have a material adverse effect on Newmont.' (the FY2014 10-K's own words; it does not call the business cyclical, so DURABLE, the MU rule); no disruption theme in the registry is live for a gold miner on this date (of the live themes, OFFSHORE is scoped to 'lower-cost offshore delivery (Indian IT services) takes share and price from Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing', CLOUD to 'public cloud displaces on-premise hardware, storage, legacy databases and data-center outsourcing', ECOMMERCE to 'e-commerce (Amazon effect) displaces physical retail, malls, grocery, distribution': none names a miner), so the watch list is empty

(the FY2014 10-K's own words; it does not call the business cyclical, so DURABLE, the MU rule); no disruption theme in the registry is live for a gold miner on this date (of the live themes, OFFSHORE is scoped to 'lower-cost offshore delivery (Indian IT services) takes share and price from Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing', CLOUD to 'public cloud displaces on-premise hardware, storage, legacy databases and data-center outsourcing', ECOMMERCE to 'e-commerce (Amazon effect) displaces physical retail, malls, grocery, distribution': none names a miner), so the watch list is empty. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.51x; +45% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +0.65; conservative 2yr -1%.

BEAR.desc: EPS +0.0%/yr (worst year FY05-FY14 ex-FY07 ex-FY11 ex-FY13, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS -9.0%/yr (Q4 revenue YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr ex-FY07 ex-FY11 ex-FY13 median

BULL.desc: EPS +7.0%/yr (FY05-FY14 ex-FY07 ex-FY11 ex-FY13 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +59.2%/yr (best 2-yr run FY05-FY14 ex-FY07 ex-FY11 ex-FY13, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: NEM (retrospective, 2015-04-02) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.51x (38.9% downside to Bear $13.64 / +76.0% upside to Bull $39.31) | Adj composite 2.77 vs market 2.12: gap +0.65 [UNDERVALUED] | +45% above the EPP floor $15.40 (14x FY15E $1.10) | Conservative 2-yr case: -0.6% total (-0.3%/yr) | At 20.3x FY15E the 15% hurdle price $29.54 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; revenue -7.8% YoY in Q4 2014, forward revenues -7.8% (Q4 2014 revenue growth (no revenue guide)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
